name: The St. Regis Beijing
positioning: The first St. Regis hotel in China, opened in 1997 in Beijing's diplomatic compound, with its own natural hot spring and 24-hour butler service
best_for: Travelers who want a walkable base in Beijing's embassy district near the Silk Market
Guests who want a hot spring spa and pools in the city
Travelers who value round-the-clock butler service

facts.text: The hotel is located in Beijing's quiet diplomatic compound.
Jianguomen Subway Station is about a 7-minute walk from the hotel.
Most of the embassies of Beijing's original diplomatic district and the Silk Market are within a 10-minute walk.
The Iridium Spa covers 1,500 square meters.
The hotel has a 6,000-square-meter landscaped garden and a glass-walled swimming pool.
The pools include an indoor natural hot spring pool and an indoor children's pool.
The Athletic Center includes an aerobics studio and squash courts.
Celestial Court serves traditional Cantonese favorites and has five private rooms.
The Garden Court has a buffet of Western and Asian dishes with a large seafood station.
The Press Club Bar has an American, vintage-style design.
A private St. Regis Butler is available 24 hours a day.

highlights.text: Natural hot springs rising from 1,500 meters underground flow through a filter into the hotel's Jacuzzis.
The hotel's Great Wall Bloody Mary substitutes Chinese pilsner for vodka.
It was the first St. Regis hotel in China.
Danieli's is an Italian restaurant with hand-painted murals and a domelike ceiling in a Mediterranean castle style.
Conde Nast Traveler notes a lobby with hand-painted ceilings and silk embroidery, and rooms with cherry armoires and Chinese silk upholstery.

considerations.text: Beijing Capital International Airport is about 25.6 km from the hotel, and pets are not allowed.
WhataHotel notes premium pricing and a formal atmosphere that may not suit all travelers.
